findings.summary: Committing the replay key inside the fold transaction makes a retry replay a merge whose post-fold invoice resync, credit-note sync/settle and revision append never ran, so the order's linked invoice and applied credits stay silently out of sync forever.
findings.detail:
State path, all lines in apps/api/src/orders/orders.service.ts unless noted:

1. `updateOrderItems` opens its fold transaction at :3338 and closes it at :4403. The new key write is the LAST statement inside it (:4396, `await this.recordMergeIdempotencyKey(tx, orderId, opts.idempotency);`), so the key row and the absolute-totals fold commit together.
2. Four further steps run AFTER that commit, outside it: `resyncOrderInvoicesForEdit(orderId)` (:4433) or `reconcileOrderDraftInvoice(orderId, { basis: "order" })` (:4436) — this is what brings the order's linked invoice to the new basis; a `Serializable` transaction (:4447) running `creditNotes.syncOrderCreditSelections(tx, orderId, customerId, dto.appliedCreditNotes)` (:4450) and `creditNotes.settleOrderCreditsInTx(tx, orderId)` (:4457); and `appendOrderRevision` (:4475).
3. Concrete failure: operator merges a $20 cart into customer A's $100 order with `Idempotency-Key: K` and `appliedCreditNotes: [{creditNoteId: cn1, amount: 15}]`. The fold commits (order total 120) together with the key row. The `Serializable` credit transaction at :4447 then fails with a serialization error (P2034/40001 — the realistic failure mode for `isolationLevel: "Serializable"` under concurrency). `updateOrderItems` rejects, the lock callback throws, `mapLockError` rethrows it (apps/api/src/orders/orders.controller.ts:263) and the client gets a 500.
4. The client retries with the same key and the same body. `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey` now hits the committed key row, the hash matches, and it returns the orderId; the controller returns `{ replayed: true }` (orders.controller.ts:194), which also skips the post-commit sweep (`if (!merged.replayed)`, :265) and returns `findOne(merged.orderId, user)` (:288) — HTTP 200.
5. Final state: order total 120; the linked invoice still at the pre-fold 100 basis because :4433/:4436 never re-ran; credit note cn1 never synced or settled; no OrderRevision row for the edit. The client saw 200 and stops retrying. Nothing heals it: I enumerated every `@LeaderCron` in apps/api/src and there is no order-to-invoice reconciler; `orders.cronSweepPendingOrders` (:1573) only consolidates when the customer has a second mergeable order, and in this scenario there is none.

Why no existing gate catches it: the build plan's window table row 2 ("Fold committed, then a later step inside updateOrderItems throws ... Replay, no re-fold") presents this exact window as strictly improved and the residual-risk list (items 1-6) does not mention the skipped reconciliation. Acceptance criterion 2 / test T2 assert only "exactly one fold"; no test asserts the invoice or credit state after a replay. Pre-fix the retry re-ran the reconcile (against a doubled 140 order) — the fix trades a loud wrong number for a silent, permanent order-vs-invoice money discrepancy, which is a residual the plan never accepted.
findings.fixHint: Decide what a replay of a request whose post-fold steps failed should do. Options: (a) on a table-hit replay, re-run the idempotent tail (`reconcileOrderDraftInvoice(orderId, {basis:"order"})` plus the credit sync/settle) before returning, so the replay converges the derived money state; (b) record durable completion separately from the fold (e.g. a `completedAt`/`stage` column on OrderIdempotencyKey, set after the tail succeeds) and treat a key row whose tail never completed as "resume the tail", not "replay"; (c) at minimum, document it as an accepted residual and add a test pinning the resulting invoice state. Do not simply move the key write back outside the transaction — that reinstates B215.
findings.decision: The evidence pins the key write as the last statement inside the fold tx (:4396) with invoice resync, credit-note sync/settle and revision append all running after commit (:4433-:4475); a process death between commit and those steps makes the same-key retry hit the replay-first read and return the order without ever bringing the linked invoice or credits to the folded basis. This is the exact retry scenario B215 exists to serve, and it touches money state, so the replay path must re-run the idempotent post-fold reconcile (or the run must document why it may not).

findings.summary: The fix enrolled the new tenant-scoped table in the PARKED RLS migration's two arrays but not in apply-rls.js's TENANT_TABLES, which is the documented step that actually arms RLS in production, so OrderIdempotencyKey is the only table on the order graph left with no RLS policy and no FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
findings.detail:
`git diff HEAD -- apps/api/prisma/deferred-rls/20260909000000_rls/migration.sql` in this worktree shows both hardcoded arrays in the PARKED RLS migration were updated to include `'OrderIdempotencyKey'` (inserted after `'OrderItem'` at the two list sites). The live sibling was missed.

apps/api/scripts/apply-rls.js declares its own hardcoded `const TENANT_TABLES = [` at :13; `"Order"` is at :30 and `"OrderItem"` at :31, and `grep -n OrderIdempotencyKey apps/api/scripts/apply-rls.js` returns nothing — the new table is absent. For every name in that array the script runs (`applyRls`, :74-86): `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ... USING ("tenantId"::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true) OR ...)`. A table not in the array gets none of that.

This script is the live production step, not a parked one: apps/api/docs/production-setup.md:107 is the literal command `node apps/api/scripts/apply-rls.js`, and its go-live checklist at :179 reads "RLS applied to all 52 tenant-scoped tables (`apply-rls.js`)".

Failure scenario: the owner runs the documented production-setup step after this change ships. Every sibling on the order graph (Order, OrderItem, OrderRevision, Invoice, ...) comes out with `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and a `tenant_isolation` policy; `OrderIdempotencyKey` silently does not (it is not even reported as skipped — the loop never names it). Any future code path that reaches this table without going through `prisma.forTenant()` / `_wrapTxWithTenant` — a raw `$queryRaw` report, a repair script, a psql session — reads and writes it across tenants with no database-layer backstop, while the identical query against Order would be blocked. Nothing in the repo will flag the omission: `grep -rn TENANT_TABLES` across apps/api/src, apps/api/scripts and scripts/ finds no spec pinning that array against the schema, so `npm run verify` stays green. The checklist's "52 tenant-scoped tables" is also now off by one.
findings.fixHint: Add `"OrderIdempotencyKey",` to `TENANT_TABLES` in apps/api/scripts/apply-rls.js immediately after `"OrderItem",` (:31), matching where it was inserted in both arrays of apps/api/prisma/deferred-rls/20260909000000_rls/migration.sql, and bump the "52 tenant-scoped tables" count in apps/api/docs/production-setup.md:179 to 53.
findings.decision: The fix round enrolled the table in both arrays of the parked deferred-rls migration but the live sibling, apply-rls.js TENANT_TABLES (:13, Order at :30, OrderItem at :31), still lacks it and a grep for the name returns nothing; every other table on the order graph gets ENABLE/FORCE RLS plus the tenant_isolation policy from that script and this one will not. A tenant-scoped table left out of the production arming step is a tenant-isolation hole the change itself created and half-fixed.

`git status --short` shows `.claude/code-map/api.md` is modified by this change, and `git diff HEAD -- .claude/code-map/api.md` shows the edits are confined to the split-script / schema-folder-spec entries (case (h) retirement, "126 model + 80 enum blocks"). So the "map updates are deferred to a Bookkeeping Option B follow-up" defence does not apply here: the map IS being updated in the code PR, just incompletely, and the result is internally inconsistent.

Concrete stale claims left behind:
- :1179 states `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey(key, customerId)` / `recordIdempotencyKey(orderId, key)` (both `forTenant()`-scoped ...). The first is now `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey, customerId, requestHash?)` (apps/api/src/orders/orders.service.ts, third param added), it now reads a new `OrderIdempotencyKey` table BEFORE the Order column, and it now THROWS in two new cases (`ForbiddenException` when the session carries no tenant; `ConflictException` on a hash mismatch and on a key already held by another order in the tenant). An agent planning from this row would call it with two arguments and assume it cannot throw.
- :2298 states `updateOrderItems(orderId, dto, user?)` (`:3069`). The signature now takes a 4th `opts?: { idempotency?: { key: string; responseHash: string } }` and the method actually starts at :3175, not :3069.
- `grep -rn "OrderIdempotencyKey|merge-idempotency|recordMergeIdempotencyKey" .claude/code-map/` returns nothing, so the map now asserts a 126-model schema folder without naming the 126th model, and the new file apps/api/src/orders/merge-idempotency.ts (`mergeRequestHash`) and the new method `recordMergeIdempotencyKey` have no entry at all.

Failure scenario: the next session follows CLAUDE.md's "read INDEX -> area -> the specific file" routine, reads :1179/:2298, and plans a change against a two-argument non-throwing lookup and a three-argument `updateOrderItems` — the exact re-derivation the map exists to prevent, on the money path this change just re-shaped.
findings.fixHint: In the same api.md edit: update :1179 to `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey(idempotencyKey, customerId, requestHash?)` noting the table-first read and the Forbidden/Conflict throws; update :2298 to `updateOrderItems(orderId, dto, user?, opts?)` and correct `:3069` to `:3175`; add a one-line entry for the `OrderIdempotencyKey` model (sales.prisma, `@@unique([tenantId, key])`, FK `onDelete: Cascade`), for `merge-idempotency.ts` (`mergeRequestHash`), and for `recordMergeIdempotencyKey` (writes through the fold tx's client, P2002 -> 409). Alternatively, revert the api.md edits entirely and carry the whole map update in the Option B follow-up the build plan specifies — but do not leave it half-updated.
findings.decision: The diff already touches .claude/code-map/api.md for the schema-spec collateral, so the Option B deferral defence does not apply, yet :1179 still records the two-argument findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey / old recordIdempotencyKey signatures and omits the new table the same map now says exists. Same-PR map update is the standing rule; this one is incomplete, not absent.

findings.summary: The new pre-fold `heldByAnotherOrder` refusal turns a staff merge that previously landed into a permanent 409 whenever the mobile client carries its cart-session key across a "Change customer" switch.
findings.detail:
REACHABLE CLIENT PATH (read, not assumed): the ONLY client that sends `Idempotency-Key` on POST /orders is mobile (apps/web has none — see the separate web finding). `apps/mobile/lib/order-submit-key.ts` mints ONE key per cart session and resets it ONLY on a successful submit or an explicit cart clear; `apps/mobile/components/NewOrderScreen.tsx:1713` rotates it on mount ONLY when `initialDraft` is null. Once the operator has added a line, `useDraftAutosave` creates a server draft and lifts its id through `onDraftBound` into the parent's `boundDraftId` (NewOrderScreen.tsx:1625-1632, :301-302), so `loadedDraft` becomes non-null and `initialDraft` is non-null (NewOrderScreen.tsx:412-421) on every later mount. `onChangeCustomer` (NewOrderScreen.tsx:405-411) unmounts/remounts ProductPickView and deliberately KEEPS the cart and the bound draft — so the key survives a customer switch.

FAILURE: (1) Operator builds a cart for customer A; Confirm -> active order exists -> prompt -> Merge -> POST with key K. The fold commits and `recordMergeIdempotencyKey` writes the row (tenant, K, ordA) INSIDE the fold tx. (2) The client never sees the 200 — the mobile api client aborts at 15s (cited in orders.controller.ts:165-167) or the request is offline-enqueued; `onError` fires, the key is deliberately NOT reset. (3) Operator taps "Change customer", picks B (cart lines carry over by design), taps Confirm -> B has an active order -> Merge -> POST key K, customerId B. (4) `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey`: the keyed lookup at :1670 is scoped `order: { customerId: B }` and misses; the new `heldByAnotherOrder` read at :1694 (`where: { key }`, tenant-scoped only, customer-agnostic) HITS the row for ordA and throws `ConflictException("Idempotency-Key already used for a different order")` at :1704. Customer B's merge never folds, and every retry from that screen repeats it — `resetOrderSubmitKey()` is unreachable without a successful submit or abandoning the cart.

PRE-CHANGE BEHAVIOUR (the regression): the merge branch's only lookup was the customer-scoped Order column (`{ idempotencyKey, customerId: B }`), which missed, so the fold RAN and B's merge landed; the post-commit column stamp's P2002 was swallowed by `recordIdempotencyKey`'s `if (e?.code !== "P2002") throw e` (orders.service.ts:1745). So this is a new hard failure on a path that previously worked. Nothing in build-plan.md or bug-test-plan.md considers a cross-customer key carried by the same cart session; no T#/D# covers it (PD1 pins only that a key recorded for one customer is not REPLAYED for another — it does not pin that the other customer's own merge still lands).
findings.fixHint: Decide what a key held by a different customer's order should do on the merge path. Options: return null (fall through to the fold, as before, and let the in-tx P2002 be the only refusal), or keep the 409 but have the mobile client rotate the key on a 409 whose message is the cross-order one, or scope the refusal so it cannot fire for a key the same cart session owns. Whatever is chosen, add a test at the T#/D# level for "same key, different customer, no prior replay".
findings.decision: The only client that sends Idempotency-Key keeps the cart-session key across a Change-customer switch and after a failed submit, so a timed-out-but-committed merge for A followed by a submit for B hits the new tenant-wide heldByAnotherOrder refusal with no recovery short of clearing the cart; the guard is correct server-side but the interaction with the one reachable client is a wedge the change introduced.

findings.summary: `heldByAnotherOrder` (tenant-wide, customer-agnostic) is evaluated BEFORE the customer-scoped Order-column fallback, so a legitimate replay of THIS customer's own key is refused with 409 instead of replayed.
findings.detail:
Read order inside `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey`: (a) :1670 key table scoped to `order: { customerId }`; (b) :1694 key table scoped to the TENANT ONLY — any order, any customer — and an unconditional 409 at :1704; (c) :1713 the Order column scoped `{ idempotencyKey, customerId }`. Step (b) short-circuits step (c), so a key that legitimately identifies THIS customer's own order via the column is never consulted once any other order in the tenant holds the same key in the table.

CONCRETE STATE PATH (reachable from the carry-over described in the sibling finding, no client uuid collision needed): (1) Customer A merges with key K; the key row (K -> ordA) commits with the fold; the post-commit column stamp is `updateMany({ where: { id, idempotencyKey: null } })` (:1741) and silently drops K because ordA already carries a key from its own creation — this "first key wins" drop is B215's original root cause, so it is the NORMAL state, not an edge case. (2) The same cart session (key K retained after a failed-looking submit) is switched to customer B, who has NO active order, so `OrdersController.create` falls through to `OrdersService.create`; create()'s pre-check at :1852 reads only the column, finds nothing (K was dropped from ordA's column), and creates ordB WITH column `idempotencyKey = K`. (3) A retry for customer B (queue replay / operator retry) now enters the merge branch because B has an active order: (a) misses (no table row for B), (b) HITS the row for ordA and throws 409 "Idempotency-Key already used for a different order" — even though (c) would have found ordB by column for this exact customer and replayed it correctly. B's retry is refused forever instead of replaying B's own order.

The code comment at :1706-1712 explicitly reasons that a column-only hit "is replay-eligible" and is "pinned by P5", but P5/T P3 only exercise the column path with NO table row present — no test covers a column hit that is pre-empted by a foreign table row, so the ordering is unproven in either direction.
findings.fixHint: Move the customer-scoped Order-column read (:1713) ABOVE the tenant-wide `heldByAnotherOrder` read (:1694), so this customer's own replay wins before any cross-order refusal; keep the cross-order refusal as the last step before the fold. Add a test with a table row for customer A plus a column key for customer B and assert B replays.
findings.decision: The read order is genuinely wrong: a tenant-wide refusal that short-circuits the customer-scoped column fallback refuses a replay that the column would have answered. It needs the same cross-customer key reuse precondition as #0, so it is a minor ordering defect to fix alongside it (consult the column before refusing).

findings.summary: `appliedCreditNotes` is fingerprinted order-sensitively while `items` is sorted, so a retry that re-sends the SAME credit-note set in a different order is refused with a 409 cart mismatch.
findings.detail:
VERIFIED BY PROBE against the real module this session (a throwaway spec under apps/api/src/orders, run with `npx jest --reporters=default`, then deleted): `ITEMS_ORDER_SAME= true`, `CREDITS_ORDER_SAME= false`. i.e. mergeRequestHash({customerId:'c1',items,appliedCreditNotes:[{creditNoteId:'cn-A'},{creditNoteId:'cn-B'}]}) !== the same call with [cn-B, cn-A]. Cause: line 28 sorts the per-item fingerprints (`(input.items ?? []).map(stable).sort()`) but line 34 passes `appliedCreditNotes` straight into `stable`, whose array branch "keeps arrays in order at this level" (comment at line 6-8). The doc comment at line 21-23 claims only "Item order does not matter" — the asymmetry is undocumented and reads as an oversight, because the server treats appliedCreditNotes as a SET: apps/mobile/lib/api/orders.ts:203-206 documents it as "the FULL desired set (server diffs)", and updateOrderItems applies a diff, so [A,B] and [B,A] are the SAME request server-side.

CONCRETE FAILURE: the operator selects credits cn-A then cn-B (mobile `onToggle` at NewOrderScreen.tsx:2359 APPENDS on select and filters on deselect, so the array order is tap order); attempt 1 posts [A,B] with key K, the fold commits and stores responseHash = H([A,B]); the client times out (15s abort) and the key is retained by design. The operator re-taps cn-A off and on again (a natural "did that credit apply?" check) — the selection is now [B,A], the same set — and taps Confirm. `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey` hits the key row at :1670, `keyed.responseHash !== requestHash` at :1675, and the retry is refused with 409 "Idempotency-Key reused with a different cart" although the request is semantically identical to the one that landed. The probe also shows `QTY_STRING_EQ_NUMBER= false` (a numeric string and a number fingerprint differently) — harmless today because both attempts traverse the same ValidationPipe, but it is the same class of brittleness.

P5/T#s cover item order, undefined-vs-null credits and a changed qty (orders.merge-idempotency.spec.ts:397-427) — credit-note ORDER is not covered, so dropping or adding a sort there leaves every test green.
findings.fixHint: Canonicalise appliedCreditNotes the same way items are: `const credits = input.appliedCreditNotes == null ? null : (input.appliedCreditNotes as readonly unknown[]).map(stable).sort();` (keeping [] distinct from null/undefined — the probe confirms `UNDEF_EQ_EMPTY= false`, which is correct since [] means "remove all"). Add a unit test pinning credit-note order-insensitivity next to the existing item-order test.
findings.decision: Probe-verified asymmetry: items are sorted, appliedCreditNotes are not, while the server treats the credit-note list as a set. A retry from unchanged client state re-sends the same order so the 409 is unlikely in practice, but the fingerprint contradicts its own doc comment and should sort both.

findings.summary: The cart-mismatch 409 tells the operator to "submit the edited cart as a new order (new key)", but the only client that sends keys cannot mint one without abandoning the cart, so an edited retry wedges the screen permanently.
findings.detail:
The new refusal at :1675-1683 is intended (bug-test-plan T3 / acceptance criterion 4). The defect is that its prescribed remedy is unreachable in the one client that reaches this code. `apps/mobile/lib/order-submit-key.ts` documents and enforces that the key resets ONLY on (a) a successful submit or (b) an explicit cart clear; a failed submit must NOT reset it. `NewOrderScreen.tsx:1817` sends `getOrderSubmitKey()` on every attempt, and the reset call sites are exactly `onSuccess` (:1823) and the mount effect (:1713) which is gated on `!initialDraft` — and R5 deliberately does NOT rotate on a resumed parked draft, precisely so a timed-out-but-committed submit stays collapsible.

FAILURE PATH: (1) merge with key K commits server-side; the client sees a timeout/offline error (mobile aborts at 15s, per orders.controller.ts:165-167) and keeps the key. (2) The operator, believing nothing landed, edits the cart (removes or re-enters a line) and taps Confirm. (3) The table row exists with H(cart1); requestHash is H(cart2); :1675 throws the 409. (4) The mobile `onError` handler has no branch for this body (it matches only `code === "MERGE_CHOICE_REQUIRED"` at :1848-1856 and the regulated-license error), so it falls to `alertInfo("Couldn't save order", msg)` and shows the server text verbatim — including "submit the edited cart as a new order (new key)", which the operator has no control to perform. Every subsequent Confirm from this screen re-sends K and repeats the 409; because the autosaved draft is bound, re-entering via the parked draft keeps `initialDraft` non-null and therefore keeps K. The only escape is discarding the draft and rebuilding the cart from scratch.

Nothing in build-plan.md or bug-test-plan.md considers what the client does with the new 409, and no test asserts a client-visible recovery path.
findings.fixHint: Either give the 409 a machine-readable code (e.g. `{ code: "IDEMPOTENCY_CART_MISMATCH" }`, the same idiom as MERGE_CHOICE_REQUIRED) and have the mobile error handler call resetOrderSubmitKey() and offer "resubmit as a new order", or have the server treat a mismatched-cart retry on the merge path as a new request (new key minted server-side) rather than a refusal. Decide before shipping; leaving it as bare text is the wedge.
findings.decision: The cart-mismatch 409 is the intended acceptance-criterion-4 refusal, and the client can recover by clearing the cart, so it is not a permanent wedge; the gap is that the mobile key lifecycle offers no graceful path (rotate on cart edit after a refusal). Client-side follow-up, not a server defect.

findings.summary: `create()`'s own replay lookup still reads only the Order column, so the new "authoritative" key table is bypassed whenever a keyed retry falls through to the create path and can still mint a duplicate order.
findings.detail:
The schema doc-comment (sales.prisma, OrderIdempotencyKey) and the migration header call the new table the store that the merge branch's replay depends on, and orders.service.ts:1685-1687 calls it "the authoritative replay store for the merge branch". But create() — the other consumer of the same client-chosen key — never reads it: its pre-check at :1852 is `order.findFirst({ where: { idempotencyKey } })` (column only), and so is its P2002 recovery at :2441. There is no production caller of `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey` other than orders.controller.ts:188 (verified: `grep -rn "findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey|recordIdempotencyKey" apps --include=*.ts` returns only that call, the :230 column stamp, and the definitions), and the buyer merge path (buyer.controller.ts:617) sends no key at all.

CONCRETE FAILURE: (1) Merge with key K lands on ordA; the key row commits with the fold; the column stamp at :1741 drops K because ordA already carries a key (the original B215 root cause, so the common case). (2) A retry of that same frozen body arrives after ordA has left the active set (consolidated away by a sweep, dispatched, or status-advanced), so `findActiveOrder` returns null and the controller never enters the merge branch (orders.controller.ts:111-113, and the explicit "stale" fall-through at :259-265). (3) `OrdersService.create` runs with the same key: its column-only pre-check finds nothing, so it creates a SECOND order for the same cart and stamps K on the new order's column. The table row that would have identified the retry is never read.

This outcome is the same before and after the change (pre-fix the key was nowhere at all), so it is a scope gap rather than a regression — but it contradicts the "authoritative replay store" framing the diff's own comments assert, and the fix had the table in hand at :1852.
findings.fixHint: Either have create()'s pre-check also consult OrderIdempotencyKey (customer-scoped, mirroring :1670) and replay/refuse from it, or soften the "authoritative" claims in sales.prisma / migration.sql / orders.service.ts:1685 to "authoritative for the merge branch only" and record the create fall-through as a known residual.
findings.decision: create()'s pre-check and P2002 recovery read only the Order column, and the column stamp is silently dropped when the target order already carries a key, so a keyed retry that no longer takes the merge branch (pending order dispatched between attempts) misses the table row and mints a duplicate. The table is authoritative only on one of two consumers of the same key.

findings.summary: This fix branch carries no lessons entry and the register is already at BOTH caps, so the required entry cannot simply be appended and Gate 3 of the stop hook will block.
findings.detail:
MEASURED THIS SESSION in the worktree: `git status --short` shows `.claude/code-map/api.md` modified (Gate 2 satisfied) but `.claude/lessons/*` untouched; `git rev-list --count master..HEAD` is 0, so everything is still working-tree and the branch is `fix/train4-order-idempotency-key`. CLAUDE.md's lessons routine states Gate 3 of `.claude/hooks/stop.mjs` blocks the turn on `fix/*` branches and on landed `fix:` commits unless the register changed in the same PR or HEAD carries a `Bookkeeping-Follow-Up: pending` trailer (the Option B exception is reserved for public-window deploys).

The non-obvious part: the register is at BOTH caps, so an append cannot succeed as-is. Measured from `.claude/lessons/_meta.json` and the file itself: `maxEntries: 40`, `maxBytes: 40960`; the file contains exactly 40 active `L-###` entries and is 40,889 bytes — 71 bytes of headroom against the byte cap and zero against the entry cap, with `nextId: 104`. `scripts/validate-lessons.mjs` enforces both (DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES = 40 at :88, the meta override read at :122-123). A typical entry is several hundred bytes, so close-out will fail the validator (and the global routine notes closeout.mjs refuses to add a stub at cap) unless an entry is archived to ARCHIVE.md first. Note also that `.claude/lessons/LESSONS-DIGEST.md` is not tracked at all (`git ls-files .claude/lessons/` lists only ARCHIVE.md, LESSONS.md, _meta.json), so it must be regenerated, not edited.
findings.fixHint: Before writing the B215 entry: move the least-cited fully-guarded entry (or merge two overlapping ones) from LESSONS.md to ARCHIVE.md, then append L-104 (Symptom / Root cause / Lesson / Guard), bump _meta.json (nextId/updatedAt), regenerate the digest with `node scripts/validate-lessons.mjs --digest`, and land it in this PR.
findings.decision: Measured: fix/* branch, lessons register untouched and at both caps (40 entries, 71 bytes headroom), so Gate 3 of the stop hook blocks the landing and a plain append cannot succeed. The close-out must archive one fully-guarded entry to ARCHIVE.md, add the B215 lesson, bump _meta.json and regenerate the digest in the same PR.

Either way EXPECTED_BLOCK_COUNT's dual use (live folder count vs original-ref proof) needs splitting. Owner/coordinator call, since it changes what a standing guard asserts.

confirmedFindings.summary: The Order-column fallback ignores requestHash and has no negative test, so acceptance criterion 4 ("same key with a different cart is refused") holds only on the table path.

confirmedFindings.summary: For a tenant-less staff caller the new tenant guard fires only after the whole fold has been computed inside the transaction, and the replay lookup that runs before it queries the new key table on the UNSCOPED client.
confirmedFindings.detail: `recordMergeIdempotencyKey` throws `ForbiddenException("Idempotency-Key requires a tenant-scoped session")` (line 1726) as the last statement of updateOrderItems' fold transaction. That condition is reachable: `RolesGuard`'s hierarchy lets TENANT_ADMIN satisfy `@Roles(OPERATOR)` on `POST /orders`, and `isStaff` in orders.controller.ts:106 is true for TENANT_ADMIN — while apps/api/prisma/deferred-rls/README.md records that production holds 3 TENANT_ADMIN users with a NULL tenantId (called out there as a data defect). For such a caller sending an Idempotency-Key (the mobile client always does), the merge branch now: (1) runs `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey`, whose `this.prisma.forTenant()` returns the UNSCOPED client when getTenantId() is null (prisma.service.ts:298-299), so the new `orderIdempotencyKey.findFirst({ where: { key, order: { customerId } } })` searches every tenant's key rows and a hit is replayed through `findOne` — the same unscoped shape the pre-existing Order-column lookup had, now extended to the new table; and (2) computes the entire fold (stock settle, credit guard, line writes, order.update) before the guard rolls it all back as a 403. `create()` guards the identical condition BEFORE any work (orders.service.ts:1760, with a comment stating exactly this unscoped-lookup reason), so the merge path is inconsistent with it: a keyed merge that previously committed now 403s after doing all the work, and the unscoped read happens ahead of the guard rather than behind it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Hoist the tenant check to the front of the merge path — refuse `idempotencyKey && !getTenantId()` in OrdersController.create's merge branch (or at the top of the branch's lock callback, before findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey), mirroring orders.service.ts:1760 — and keep the in-tx guard as the fail-closed backstop. That both avoids the wasted/rolled-back fold and stops the unscoped key-table read from running at all.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new tenant-scoped OrderIdempotencyKey table is absent from both hardcoded table arrays in the parked RLS arming migration, and nothing in the repo will flag the omission.
confirmedFindings.detail: The parked arming migration enumerates every tenant-scoped table twice as literal arrays — the ALTER/CREATE POLICY loop (line 26) and the verification block that RAISEs unless all three properties landed (line 114). `OrderIdempotencyKey` appears in neither, while its sibling `Order`/`OrderItem` do. Because the verification block re-checks only its own hardcoded list, the day the owner arms RLS this table silently ends up with `relrowsecurity = false` and no policy while every other tenant-scoped table is covered, and the migration still exits 0 — the gap is invisible rather than loud. Note this is a plan-sanctioned exclusion, not an oversight by the implementer: build-plan.md's scope fence lists "appending the table to the parked RLS list (apps/api/prisma/deferred-rls/)" as out of scope, so whether to close it here is the owner's call. Flagging it because the omission is durable and nothing else records it. App-level tenant scoping is in place today (`forTenant()` injects tenantId on findFirst, the tx proxy on create/updateMany), so there is no exploitable gap now — RLS is unarmed in production.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either append 'OrderIdempotencyKey' to both arrays (lines ~26 and ~114) of the parked migration — it arms nothing, the file lives outside prisma/migrations/ — or record the omission where the arming checklist lives so the pre-flight catches it. Do not arm anything: owner rule D3 gates that.

confirmedFindings.summary: Both new 409 guard paths throw with no log line and no Sentry event, so the fold-aborting failure they introduce leaves nothing in the logs to diagnose at 2am.
confirmedFindings.detail: recordMergeIdempotencyKey's P2002 branch (orders.service.ts:1734) throws `ConflictException("Idempotency-Key already used for a different order")` from inside the fold transaction, and findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey's hash-mismatch branch (orders.service.ts:1667) throws `ConflictException("Idempotency-Key reused with a different cart ...")`. Neither logs. I read apps/api/src/common/sentry-exception.filter.ts:14: `if (status >= 500)` — a 409 is never captured, and Nest's default filter does not log HttpExceptions, so there is no tenant/customer/order/key trace for either event. The comment this change rewrote (orders.controller.ts, the kept recordIdempotencyKey try/catch) still logs its far less consequential failure with full context (`idempotency record failed after merge commit tenant=... customer=... order=... key=...`). The build plan's Observability section asserts "A 409 'Idempotency-Key reused with a different cart' or 'already used for a different order' on POST /orders means the new guard fired" — true of the HTTP status only; nothing server-side records which tenant, customer, order or key, and the P2002 case also silently rolled a fold back.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Log a warn (tenant/customer/order/key, and which of the two guards fired) at the throw sites, mirroring the existing logger.error line on the column-stamp path, so the 409 is greppable.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new in-transaction key insert can abort the fold after revertLinkedInvoicesForOrderEdit has already committed outside it, leaving a linked invoice flipped SENT->DRAFT for an order edit that never landed.
confirmedFindings.detail: orders.service.ts:3232 calls `await this.invoicesService.revertLinkedInvoicesForOrderEdit(orderId)` with no tx argument, so it runs on this.prisma.forTenant() and commits on its own connection, 62 lines before the fold transaction opens at 3294. invoices.service.ts:4338 shows what it writes: each linked SENT/VIEWED/OVERDUE non-delivery-batch invoice is updated to `status: DRAFT, sentAt: null, pdfUrl: null` plus a '[... reverted to Draft: source order edited]' note. The new key insert at orders.service.ts:4352 is the last statement of the fold transaction, so a P2002 (a key already held by another customer's order in the same tenant, the case D3 proves) throws, the fold rolls back, and the post-transaction reconcile/resync never runs — the order is byte-identical but its invoice is left reverted to DRAFT with sentAt/pdfUrl cleared, and the operator gets a 409. The build plan's window table presents this abort as clean ('the fold never lands'), which is true of the fold and not of the pre-transaction invoice revert. Reachability is narrow (needs a cross-customer key collision AND a SENT pending-mirror on the merge target), and the same partial-failure shape already exists for other in-transaction throws (credit/stock guards) — this change adds a new trigger for it rather than creating it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide whether to move the cross-customer key check ahead of the fold (an unscoped-by-customer (tenantId,key) lookup inside the lock, 409 before any write) so the only in-transaction insert left is the one that cannot collide, or to accept and document that a 409'd merge can leave a reverted invoice.

confirmedFindings.summary: T5's oracle cannot distinguish the fold transaction's client from the root Prisma client, so acceptance criterion 3 (the key row is written THROUGH the fold tx) is asserted by no test.
confirmedFindings.detail: In apps/api/src/testing/prisma-mock.ts, `forTenant: jest.fn().mockReturnValue(models)` and `tenantTransaction: jest.fn((fn) => fn({ ...models, $executeRaw, $queryRaw }))` — the spread copies property references, so `tx.orderIdempotencyKey.create`, `prisma.forTenant().orderIdempotencyKey.create` and `prisma.orderIdempotencyKey.create` are the SAME jest.fn. T5 only records `openTx` at call time, and T4 only inspects `prisma.orderIdempotencyKey.create.mock.calls`. Concrete surviving mutation: change orders.service.ts:4352 from `this.recordMergeIdempotencyKey(tx, ...)` to `this.recordMergeIdempotencyKey(this.prisma.forTenant(), ...)`. That is exactly the defect the plan's Risk table calls out ("Edit 4 lands outside the fold tx") — in production it writes on a different connection, so the key commits independently of the fold and the double-fold window returns — yet T4, T5 and T10 all stay green, and the whole unit lane stays green. D3 does not close it either: order-idempotency-key.db.spec.ts:115 passes a `tx` the TEST opened, so it proves only that recordMergeIdempotencyKey honours whatever client it is handed, never that updateOrderItems hands it its own. No test in the suite fails if the fold and the key stop being atomic.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Make the tx client distinguishable in T5: have the tenantTransaction override hand the callback a tx whose `orderIdempotencyKey.create` is a DISTINCT jest.fn from `prisma.orderIdempotencyKey.create` (e.g. `{ ...prisma, orderIdempotencyKey: { ...prisma.orderIdempotencyKey, create: txCreate } }`), then assert `txCreate` was called and the root `prisma.orderIdempotencyKey.create` was not. Alternatively add a DB-lane test that drives the real `updateOrderItems` and proves rollback of fold+key together.

confirmedFindings.summary: D1's and PD1's oracle calls run outside tenantCtx.run, so the replay lookup they assert on executes through the UNSCOPED Prisma client, not the tenant-scoped path production uses.
confirmedFindings.detail: `mergeOnce` correctly wraps its work in `tenantCtx.run(f.tenantId, …)` (line 110), but the assertions at line 152 (D1) and line 177 (PD1) call `svc.findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey(...)` directly, outside any `tenantCtx.run`. `PrismaService.forTenant()` (prisma.service.ts:296-299) returns the UNSCOPED `this` when `tenantCtx.getOrNull()` is null, so the new `orderIdempotencyKey.findFirst` in the code under test runs with `where: { key, order: { customerId } }` and no `tenantId` predicate. Both tests still pass for the right reason (D1's row exists; PD1's row belongs to another customer, and the `order: { customerId }` relation filter is what excludes it), so no assertion is wrong — but the test plan lists PD1 as the proof for acceptance criterion 5 and D1 as the proof that the table-first replay works, and neither exercises the tenant-scoped read that production takes. If the `forTenant()` scoping of the new delegate were broken, D1 and PD1 would both still be green. D2's second `mergeOnce` and PD2 do cover the scoped read, so the criterion is not wholly untested — the two named tests are just weaker evidence than the matrix implies.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Wrap the two oracle calls in `tenantCtx.run(a.tenantId, () => svc.findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey(...))` so they run the same scoped path as mergeOnce; while there, consider making PD1 (or a sibling pin) assert cross-TENANT isolation of the key table explicitly, since nothing currently does.

confirmedFindings.summary: Nothing covers mergeRequestHash's documented order-insensitivity, so dropping the `.sort()` in merge-idempotency.ts leaves every test green.
confirmedFindings.detail: merge-idempotency.ts:28 (`(input.items ?? []).map(stable).sort()`) and its JSDoc claim "Item order does not matter". No test calls mergeRequestHash directly, and the only test that exercises differing carts is T3, which changes the QUANTITY (mergeDto(5) vs mergeDto(7)) — those hash differently with or without the sort. Concrete surviving mutation: delete `.sort()`. All 14 tests stay green (verified by inspection: T1/T2/P1/P2 send byte-identical dtos, T3 sends different quantities), but in production a legitimate retry whose queued payload re-serialises the same cart in a different item order now fingerprints differently and is answered with 409 "Idempotency-Key reused with a different cart" instead of being replayed.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add a direct unit test on mergeRequestHash: two inputs with the same items in reversed order must hash equal, and a changed qty must hash differently.

confirmedFindings.summary: recordMergeIdempotencyKey's tenant guard and its non-P2002 rethrow are both untested — only the P2002 branch has a case (T10).
confirmedFindings.detail: orders.service.ts:1724-1726 throws ForbiddenException when `this.prisma.getTenantId()` is falsy (the guard that stops an untenanted SUPER_ADMIN merge from writing a key row with no tenant scope), and orders.service.ts:1738 rethrows any non-P2002 error so the fold aborts rather than silently continuing. createMockPrisma's `getTenantId` always returns "test-tenant", so the guard branch is unreachable in the current harness and no test drives a non-P2002 rejection. Concrete surviving mutations: delete the `if (!tenantId) throw ...` block, or replace the final `throw e` with `return` — all 14 tests stay green, while in production the first case writes a cross-tenant-visible row under an unscoped session and the second swallows a Postgres error inside an open transaction (Landmine 1 of the plan: every subsequent statement then fails with "current transaction is aborted").
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add two cases to the T4 harness: `(prisma as any).getTenantId.mockReturnValue(null)` expecting ForbiddenException, and an `orderIdempotencyKey.create` rejection with no `code` expecting that same error to propagate (not a ConflictException).

confirmedFindings.summary: mergeOnce still guards the key write behind `typeof svc.recordMergeIdempotencyKey === "function"`, a branch whose false side nothing can execute now that the method exists.
confirmedFindings.detail: The guard existed so the spec could run red against the pre-fix tree. Post-fix the false branch is dead, and it makes the DB lane fail soft rather than fast: if recordMergeIdempotencyKey is ever renamed or removed, mergeOnce silently stops writing key rows, so pins PD1 and PD2 (which only need "folded once each") stay GREEN and report the lane healthy while the feature under test is gone — only D1-D3 go red. A pin that can pass through a dead branch is not pinning what its title claims.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Drop the `typeof` guard and call `svc.recordMergeIdempotencyKey(tx, ...)` unconditionally, so a missing method fails every test in the lane immediately.

confirmedFindings.summary: Test "REG-B215 T3" did not fail when apps/api/src/orders/merge-idempotency.ts was deliberately broken — it does not actually cover this behavior
confirmedFindings.detail: Protected behavior: identical carts hash equal. Injected defect: Dropped the `.sort()` in mergeRequestHash's item normalization (`(input.items ?? []).map(stable).sort()` -> `.map(stable)`), so two identical carts whose items arrive in a different order no longer hash equal.. Result: REG-B215 T3 PASSED with the defect in place: `npx jest src/orders/orders.merge-idempotency.spec.ts -t "REG-B215 T3"` -> "PASS src/orders/orders.merge-idempotency.spec.ts / √ REG-B215 T3: the same key with a different cart is refused, never folded (8 ms) ... Tests: 13 skipped, 1 passed, 14 total". T3 is structurally blind to "identical carts hash equal": it sends two DIFFERENT carts (qty 5 then qty 7) under one key and asserts only that the second rejects with ConflictException. Any mutation that makes equal carts hash UNequal still leaves unequal carts hashing unequal, so the conflict still fires and T3 stays green. The named behavior is pinned by T1/T2 (same-key retry with an identical cart must fold once, i.e. must be replayed), not by T3. Restore verified: post-restore sha256 equals preHash and `cmp -s` against the temp backup reported IDENTICAL before the backup was deleted.. The test is passing for a reason other than the behavior it claims to prove.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Strengthen or add the test so this exact defect turns it red; do not weaken the implementation to match a weak test.

plan.note: Round 1 fixes everything but #0, in one wave (the service, its unit spec and the DB spec are all cross-dependent so they must co-land). remainingFindings.summary: Committing the replay key inside the fold transaction makes a retry replay a merge whose post-fold invoice resync, credit-note sync/settle and revision append never ran, so the order's linked invoice and applied credits stay silently out of sync forever.
remainingFindings.detail:
State path, all lines in apps/api/src/orders/orders.service.ts unless noted:

1. `updateOrderItems` opens its fold transaction at :3338 and closes it at :4403. The new key write is the LAST statement inside it (:4396, `await this.recordMergeIdempotencyKey(tx, orderId, opts.idempotency);`), so the key row and the absolute-totals fold commit together.
2. Four further steps run AFTER that commit, outside it: `resyncOrderInvoicesForEdit(orderId)` (:4433) or `reconcileOrderDraftInvoice(orderId, { basis: "order" })` (:4436) — this is what brings the order's linked invoice to the new basis; a `Serializable` transaction (:4447) running `creditNotes.syncOrderCreditSelections(tx, orderId, customerId, dto.appliedCreditNotes)` (:4450) and `creditNotes.settleOrderCreditsInTx(tx, orderId)` (:4457); and `appendOrderRevision` (:4475).
3. Concrete failure: operator merges a $20 cart into customer A's $100 order with `Idempotency-Key: K` and `appliedCreditNotes: [{creditNoteId: cn1, amount: 15}]`. The fold commits (order total 120) together with the key row. The `Serializable` credit transaction at :4447 then fails with a serialization error (P2034/40001 — the realistic failure mode for `isolationLevel: "Serializable"` under concurrency). `updateOrderItems` rejects, the lock callback throws, `mapLockError` rethrows it (apps/api/src/orders/orders.controller.ts:263) and the client gets a 500.
4. The client retries with the same key and the same body. `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey` now hits the committed key row, the hash matches, and it returns the orderId; the controller returns `{ replayed: true }` (orders.controller.ts:194), which also skips the post-commit sweep (`if (!merged.replayed)`, :265) and returns `findOne(merged.orderId, user)` (:288) — HTTP 200.
5. Final state: order total 120; the linked invoice still at the pre-fold 100 basis because :4433/:4436 never re-ran; credit note cn1 never synced or settled; no OrderRevision row for the edit. The client saw 200 and stops retrying. Nothing heals it: I enumerated every `@LeaderCron` in apps/api/src and there is no order-to-invoice reconciler; `orders.cronSweepPendingOrders` (:1573) only consolidates when the customer has a second mergeable order, and in this scenario there is none.

Why no existing gate catches it: the build plan's window table row 2 ("Fold committed, then a later step inside updateOrderItems throws ... Replay, no re-fold") presents this exact window as strictly improved and the residual-risk list (items 1-6) does not mention the skipped reconciliation. Acceptance criterion 2 / test T2 assert only "exactly one fold"; no test asserts the invoice or credit state after a replay. Pre-fix the retry re-ran the reconcile (against a doubled 140 order) — the fix trades a loud wrong number for a silent, permanent order-vs-invoice money discrepancy, which is a residual the plan never accepted.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Decide what a replay of a request whose post-fold steps failed should do. Options: (a) on a table-hit replay, re-run the idempotent tail (`reconcileOrderDraftInvoice(orderId, {basis:"order"})` plus the credit sync/settle) before returning, so the replay converges the derived money state; (b) record durable completion separately from the fold (e.g. a `completedAt`/`stage` column on OrderIdempotencyKey, set after the tail succeeds) and treat a key row whose tail never completed as "resume the tail", not "replay"; (c) at minimum, document it as an accepted residual and add a test pinning the resulting invoice state. Do not simply move the key write back outside the transaction — that reinstates B215.
remainingFindings.decision: The evidence pins the key write as the last statement inside the fold tx (:4396) with invoice resync, credit-note sync/settle and revision append all running after commit (:4433-:4475); a process death between commit and those steps makes the same-key retry hit the replay-first read and return the order without ever bringing the linked invoice or credits to the folded basis. This is the exact retry scenario B215 exists to serve, and it touches money state, so the replay path must re-run the idempotent post-fold reconcile (or the run must document why it may not).

remainingFindings.summary: The new pre-fold `heldByAnotherOrder` refusal turns a staff merge that previously landed into a permanent 409 whenever the mobile client carries its cart-session key across a "Change customer" switch.
remainingFindings.detail:
REACHABLE CLIENT PATH (read, not assumed): the ONLY client that sends `Idempotency-Key` on POST /orders is mobile (apps/web has none — see the separate web finding). `apps/mobile/lib/order-submit-key.ts` mints ONE key per cart session and resets it ONLY on a successful submit or an explicit cart clear; `apps/mobile/components/NewOrderScreen.tsx:1713` rotates it on mount ONLY when `initialDraft` is null. Once the operator has added a line, `useDraftAutosave` creates a server draft and lifts its id through `onDraftBound` into the parent's `boundDraftId` (NewOrderScreen.tsx:1625-1632, :301-302), so `loadedDraft` becomes non-null and `initialDraft` is non-null (NewOrderScreen.tsx:412-421) on every later mount. `onChangeCustomer` (NewOrderScreen.tsx:405-411) unmounts/remounts ProductPickView and deliberately KEEPS the cart and the bound draft — so the key survives a customer switch.

FAILURE: (1) Operator builds a cart for customer A; Confirm -> active order exists -> prompt -> Merge -> POST with key K. The fold commits and `recordMergeIdempotencyKey` writes the row (tenant, K, ordA) INSIDE the fold tx. (2) The client never sees the 200 — the mobile api client aborts at 15s (cited in orders.controller.ts:165-167) or the request is offline-enqueued; `onError` fires, the key is deliberately NOT reset. (3) Operator taps "Change customer", picks B (cart lines carry over by design), taps Confirm -> B has an active order -> Merge -> POST key K, customerId B. (4) `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey`: the keyed lookup at :1670 is scoped `order: { customerId: B }` and misses; the new `heldByAnotherOrder` read at :1694 (`where: { key }`, tenant-scoped only, customer-agnostic) HITS the row for ordA and throws `ConflictException("Idempotency-Key already used for a different order")` at :1704. Customer B's merge never folds, and every retry from that screen repeats it — `resetOrderSubmitKey()` is unreachable without a successful submit or abandoning the cart.

PRE-CHANGE BEHAVIOUR (the regression): the merge branch's only lookup was the customer-scoped Order column (`{ idempotencyKey, customerId: B }`), which missed, so the fold RAN and B's merge landed; the post-commit column stamp's P2002 was swallowed by `recordIdempotencyKey`'s `if (e?.code !== "P2002") throw e` (orders.service.ts:1745). So this is a new hard failure on a path that previously worked. Nothing in build-plan.md or bug-test-plan.md considers a cross-customer key carried by the same cart session; no T#/D# covers it (PD1 pins only that a key recorded for one customer is not REPLAYED for another — it does not pin that the other customer's own merge still lands).
remainingFindings.fixHint: Decide what a key held by a different customer's order should do on the merge path. Options: return null (fall through to the fold, as before, and let the in-tx P2002 be the only refusal), or keep the 409 but have the mobile client rotate the key on a 409 whose message is the cross-order one, or scope the refusal so it cannot fire for a key the same cart session owns. Whatever is chosen, add a test at the T#/D# level for "same key, different customer, no prior replay".
remainingFindings.decision: The only client that sends Idempotency-Key keeps the cart-session key across a Change-customer switch and after a failed submit, so a timed-out-but-committed merge for A followed by a submit for B hits the new tenant-wide heldByAnotherOrder refusal with no recovery short of clearing the cart; the guard is correct server-side but the interaction with the one reachable client is a wedge the change introduced.

remainingFindings.summary: `heldByAnotherOrder` (tenant-wide, customer-agnostic) is evaluated BEFORE the customer-scoped Order-column fallback, so a legitimate replay of THIS customer's own key is refused with 409 instead of replayed.
remainingFindings.detail:
Read order inside `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey`: (a) :1670 key table scoped to `order: { customerId }`; (b) :1694 key table scoped to the TENANT ONLY — any order, any customer — and an unconditional 409 at :1704; (c) :1713 the Order column scoped `{ idempotencyKey, customerId }`. Step (b) short-circuits step (c), so a key that legitimately identifies THIS customer's own order via the column is never consulted once any other order in the tenant holds the same key in the table.

CONCRETE STATE PATH (reachable from the carry-over described in the sibling finding, no client uuid collision needed): (1) Customer A merges with key K; the key row (K -> ordA) commits with the fold; the post-commit column stamp is `updateMany({ where: { id, idempotencyKey: null } })` (:1741) and silently drops K because ordA already carries a key from its own creation — this "first key wins" drop is B215's original root cause, so it is the NORMAL state, not an edge case. (2) The same cart session (key K retained after a failed-looking submit) is switched to customer B, who has NO active order, so `OrdersController.create` falls through to `OrdersService.create`; create()'s pre-check at :1852 reads only the column, finds nothing (K was dropped from ordA's column), and creates ordB WITH column `idempotencyKey = K`. (3) A retry for customer B (queue replay / operator retry) now enters the merge branch because B has an active order: (a) misses (no table row for B), (b) HITS the row for ordA and throws 409 "Idempotency-Key already used for a different order" — even though (c) would have found ordB by column for this exact customer and replayed it correctly. B's retry is refused forever instead of replaying B's own order.

The code comment at :1706-1712 explicitly reasons that a column-only hit "is replay-eligible" and is "pinned by P5", but P5/T P3 only exercise the column path with NO table row present — no test covers a column hit that is pre-empted by a foreign table row, so the ordering is unproven in either direction.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Move the customer-scoped Order-column read (:1713) ABOVE the tenant-wide `heldByAnotherOrder` read (:1694), so this customer's own replay wins before any cross-order refusal; keep the cross-order refusal as the last step before the fold. Add a test with a table row for customer A plus a column key for customer B and assert B replays.
remainingFindings.decision: The read order is genuinely wrong: a tenant-wide refusal that short-circuits the customer-scoped column fallback refuses a replay that the column would have answered. It needs the same cross-customer key reuse precondition as #0, so it is a minor ordering defect to fix alongside it (consult the column before refusing).

remainingFindings.summary: `appliedCreditNotes` is fingerprinted order-sensitively while `items` is sorted, so a retry that re-sends the SAME credit-note set in a different order is refused with a 409 cart mismatch.
remainingFindings.detail:
VERIFIED BY PROBE against the real module this session (a throwaway spec under apps/api/src/orders, run with `npx jest --reporters=default`, then deleted): `ITEMS_ORDER_SAME= true`, `CREDITS_ORDER_SAME= false`. i.e. mergeRequestHash({customerId:'c1',items,appliedCreditNotes:[{creditNoteId:'cn-A'},{creditNoteId:'cn-B'}]}) !== the same call with [cn-B, cn-A]. Cause: line 28 sorts the per-item fingerprints (`(input.items ?? []).map(stable).sort()`) but line 34 passes `appliedCreditNotes` straight into `stable`, whose array branch "keeps arrays in order at this level" (comment at line 6-8). The doc comment at line 21-23 claims only "Item order does not matter" — the asymmetry is undocumented and reads as an oversight, because the server treats appliedCreditNotes as a SET: apps/mobile/lib/api/orders.ts:203-206 documents it as "the FULL desired set (server diffs)", and updateOrderItems applies a diff, so [A,B] and [B,A] are the SAME request server-side.

CONCRETE FAILURE: the operator selects credits cn-A then cn-B (mobile `onToggle` at NewOrderScreen.tsx:2359 APPENDS on select and filters on deselect, so the array order is tap order); attempt 1 posts [A,B] with key K, the fold commits and stores responseHash = H([A,B]); the client times out (15s abort) and the key is retained by design. The operator re-taps cn-A off and on again (a natural "did that credit apply?" check) — the selection is now [B,A], the same set — and taps Confirm. `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey` hits the key row at :1670, `keyed.responseHash !== requestHash` at :1675, and the retry is refused with 409 "Idempotency-Key reused with a different cart" although the request is semantically identical to the one that landed. The probe also shows `QTY_STRING_EQ_NUMBER= false` (a numeric string and a number fingerprint differently) — harmless today because both attempts traverse the same ValidationPipe, but it is the same class of brittleness.

P5/T#s cover item order, undefined-vs-null credits and a changed qty (orders.merge-idempotency.spec.ts:397-427) — credit-note ORDER is not covered, so dropping or adding a sort there leaves every test green.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Canonicalise appliedCreditNotes the same way items are: `const credits = input.appliedCreditNotes == null ? null : (input.appliedCreditNotes as readonly unknown[]).map(stable).sort();` (keeping [] distinct from null/undefined — the probe confirms `UNDEF_EQ_EMPTY= false`, which is correct since [] means "remove all"). Add a unit test pinning credit-note order-insensitivity next to the existing item-order test.
remainingFindings.decision: Probe-verified asymmetry: items are sorted, appliedCreditNotes are not, while the server treats the credit-note list as a set. A retry from unchanged client state re-sends the same order so the 409 is unlikely in practice, but the fingerprint contradicts its own doc comment and should sort both.

remainingFindings.summary: The cart-mismatch 409 tells the operator to "submit the edited cart as a new order (new key)", but the only client that sends keys cannot mint one without abandoning the cart, so an edited retry wedges the screen permanently.
remainingFindings.detail:
The new refusal at :1675-1683 is intended (bug-test-plan T3 / acceptance criterion 4). The defect is that its prescribed remedy is unreachable in the one client that reaches this code. `apps/mobile/lib/order-submit-key.ts` documents and enforces that the key resets ONLY on (a) a successful submit or (b) an explicit cart clear; a failed submit must NOT reset it. `NewOrderScreen.tsx:1817` sends `getOrderSubmitKey()` on every attempt, and the reset call sites are exactly `onSuccess` (:1823) and the mount effect (:1713) which is gated on `!initialDraft` — and R5 deliberately does NOT rotate on a resumed parked draft, precisely so a timed-out-but-committed submit stays collapsible.

FAILURE PATH: (1) merge with key K commits server-side; the client sees a timeout/offline error (mobile aborts at 15s, per orders.controller.ts:165-167) and keeps the key. (2) The operator, believing nothing landed, edits the cart (removes or re-enters a line) and taps Confirm. (3) The table row exists with H(cart1); requestHash is H(cart2); :1675 throws the 409. (4) The mobile `onError` handler has no branch for this body (it matches only `code === "MERGE_CHOICE_REQUIRED"` at :1848-1856 and the regulated-license error), so it falls to `alertInfo("Couldn't save order", msg)` and shows the server text verbatim — including "submit the edited cart as a new order (new key)", which the operator has no control to perform. Every subsequent Confirm from this screen re-sends K and repeats the 409; because the autosaved draft is bound, re-entering via the parked draft keeps `initialDraft` non-null and therefore keeps K. The only escape is discarding the draft and rebuilding the cart from scratch.

Nothing in build-plan.md or bug-test-plan.md considers what the client does with the new 409, and no test asserts a client-visible recovery path.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either give the 409 a machine-readable code (e.g. `{ code: "IDEMPOTENCY_CART_MISMATCH" }`, the same idiom as MERGE_CHOICE_REQUIRED) and have the mobile error handler call resetOrderSubmitKey() and offer "resubmit as a new order", or have the server treat a mismatched-cart retry on the merge path as a new request (new key minted server-side) rather than a refusal. Decide before shipping; leaving it as bare text is the wedge.
remainingFindings.decision: The cart-mismatch 409 is the intended acceptance-criterion-4 refusal, and the client can recover by clearing the cart, so it is not a permanent wedge; the gap is that the mobile key lifecycle offers no graceful path (rotate on cart edit after a refusal). Client-side follow-up, not a server defect.

remainingFindings.summary: `create()`'s own replay lookup still reads only the Order column, so the new "authoritative" key table is bypassed whenever a keyed retry falls through to the create path and can still mint a duplicate order.
remainingFindings.detail:
The schema doc-comment (sales.prisma, OrderIdempotencyKey) and the migration header call the new table the store that the merge branch's replay depends on, and orders.service.ts:1685-1687 calls it "the authoritative replay store for the merge branch". But create() — the other consumer of the same client-chosen key — never reads it: its pre-check at :1852 is `order.findFirst({ where: { idempotencyKey } })` (column only), and so is its P2002 recovery at :2441. There is no production caller of `findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey` other than orders.controller.ts:188 (verified: `grep -rn "findOrderIdByIdempotencyKey|recordIdempotencyKey" apps --include=*.ts` returns only that call, the :230 column stamp, and the definitions), and the buyer merge path (buyer.controller.ts:617) sends no key at all.

CONCRETE FAILURE: (1) Merge with key K lands on ordA; the key row commits with the fold; the column stamp at :1741 drops K because ordA already carries a key (the original B215 root cause, so the common case). (2) A retry of that same frozen body arrives after ordA has left the active set (consolidated away by a sweep, dispatched, or status-advanced), so `findActiveOrder` returns null and the controller never enters the merge branch (orders.controller.ts:111-113, and the explicit "stale" fall-through at :259-265). (3) `OrdersService.create` runs with the same key: its column-only pre-check finds nothing, so it creates a SECOND order for the same cart and stamps K on the new order's column. The table row that would have identified the retry is never read.

This outcome is the same before and after the change (pre-fix the key was nowhere at all), so it is a scope gap rather than a regression — but it contradicts the "authoritative replay store" framing the diff's own comments assert, and the fix had the table in hand at :1852.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either have create()'s pre-check also consult OrderIdempotencyKey (customer-scoped, mirroring :1670) and replay/refuse from it, or soften the "authoritative" claims in sales.prisma / migration.sql / orders.service.ts:1685 to "authoritative for the merge branch only" and record the create fall-through as a known residual.
remainingFindings.decision: create()'s pre-check and P2002 recovery read only the Order column, and the column stamp is silently dropped when the target order already carries a key, so a keyed retry that no longer takes the merge branch (pending order dispatched between attempts) misses the table row and mints a duplicate. The table is authoritative only on one of two consumers of the same key.

remainingFindings.summary: This fix branch carries no lessons entry and the register is already at BOTH caps, so the required entry cannot simply be appended and Gate 3 of the stop hook will block.
remainingFindings.detail:
MEASURED THIS SESSION in the worktree: `git status --short` shows `.claude/code-map/api.md` modified (Gate 2 satisfied) but `.claude/lessons/*` untouched; `git rev-list --count master..HEAD` is 0, so everything is still working-tree and the branch is `fix/train4-order-idempotency-key`. CLAUDE.md's lessons routine states Gate 3 of `.claude/hooks/stop.mjs` blocks the turn on `fix/*` branches and on landed `fix:` commits unless the register changed in the same PR or HEAD carries a `Bookkeeping-Follow-Up: pending` trailer (the Option B exception is reserved for public-window deploys).

The non-obvious part: the register is at BOTH caps, so an append cannot succeed as-is. Measured from `.claude/lessons/_meta.json` and the file itself: `maxEntries: 40`, `maxBytes: 40960`; the file contains exactly 40 active `L-###` entries and is 40,889 bytes — 71 bytes of headroom against the byte cap and zero against the entry cap, with `nextId: 104`. `scripts/validate-lessons.mjs` enforces both (DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES = 40 at :88, the meta override read at :122-123). A typical entry is several hundred bytes, so close-out will fail the validator (and the global routine notes closeout.mjs refuses to add a stub at cap) unless an entry is archived to ARCHIVE.md first. Note also that `.claude/lessons/LESSONS-DIGEST.md` is not tracked at all (`git ls-files .claude/lessons/` lists only ARCHIVE.md, LESSONS.md, _meta.json), so it must be regenerated, not edited.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Before writing the B215 entry: move the least-cited fully-guarded entry (or merge two overlapping ones) from LESSONS.md to ARCHIVE.md, then append L-104 (Symptom / Root cause / Lesson / Guard), bump _meta.json (nextId/updatedAt), regenerate the digest with `node scripts/validate-lessons.mjs --digest`, and land it in this PR.
remainingFindings.decision: Measured: fix/* branch, lessons register untouched and at both caps (40 entries, 71 bytes headroom), so Gate 3 of the stop hook blocks the landing and a plain append cannot succeed. The close-out must archive one fully-guarded entry to ARCHIVE.md, add the B215 lesson, bump _meta.json and regenerate the digest in the same PR.
